script.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.

terra.problem: The sandbox comparison uses a child-oriented play scenario, contrary to the adult-audience rule.
The passage does not say the sign appears before Ezekiel says a word.
The city is drawn on the brick; the siege works are constructed around it, not drawn on it.
The gift-and-sign joke does not make a clear comparison: a sign is not necessarily something one stands reading.
The passage does not say nobody can look at a ceiling.
A week represented by each day would not mean more days lying down. The joke's comparison does not follow the stated action.
“Counting is half the battle on this one” comments on the question rather than the passage.
The passage gives set eating times but does not say whether midnight is one of them.
The scale joke makes light of anxious eating during a serious shortage.
The text says the bread is rationed by weight, not that a scale is used.
Rationing by weight does not establish that the bread is counted out or that it is not distributed by group.
“I'm not going to joke about it” comments on how Papa Dorin tells the passage.
“I'll keep it simple” comments on how Papa Dorin tells the passage.
“I'll just say it plainly” comments on how Papa Dorin tells the passage.
